hook.message: The subject and the stake may arrive too late. The 15 words are this tool's reference for the first sentence, not a rule of the method.
hook.fix: The method asks for a hook of one to three short sentences: see if the first one can say the subject and what the viewer gets in fewer words.

rules.message: Em dash used as a pause, a common AI rhythm crutch (Floor FL1).
rules.fix: Use a comma, period, colon or parentheses.

rules.message: Filler -ly adverb that pads or intensifies (Floor FL3).
rules.fix: Cut it; the sentence is almost always stronger without it.

rules.message: "It's not X, it's Y" template: a telegraphed twist (Floor FL2).
rules.fix: State Y directly.

rules.message: "The problem isn't X, it's Y" sets up a binary contrast (Floor FL2).
rules.fix: Say what the problem is, directly.

rules.message: "X isn't the problem, Y is" template (Floor FL2).
rules.fix: Name Y and state it.

rules.message: "Not just X, but Y" sits on the fence.
rules.fix: Pick one and say it.

rules.message: "It looks like X, it's actually Y" is a textbook reveal.
rules.fix: Say what it is.

rules.message: "Stops being X and becomes Y" is a textbook transformation.
rules.fix: Tell what changed, with the concrete detail.

rules.message: "That's it. That's all." is emphasis with no content.
rules.fix: Write one complete sentence that carries information.

rules.message: "And that's okay" gives permission nobody asked for.
rules.fix: Cut it.

rules.message: A setup line that leads nowhere.
rules.fix: Cut the setup and say the thing.

rules.message: A lifeless thing acting like a person.
rules.fix: Say who acts and what they do.

rules.message: AI cliché that announces instead of starting.
rules.fix: Start with the first fact or the scene.

rules.message: "Deep dive" is corporate filler.
rules.fix: Say what you will show, or just show it.

rules.message: "Game-changer" is an empty superlative.
rules.fix: Say what changed and by how much, with a source.

rules.message: "In today's fast-paced world" is padding.
rules.fix: Put the viewer in a concrete scene instead.

rules.message: Movie-trailer padding.
rules.fix: Start with the fact.

rules.message: Throat-clearing before the point.
rules.fix: Delete it and state the point.

rules.message: Throat-clearing before the point.
rules.fix: Cut it and go straight in.

rules.message: Announcing honesty is throat-clearing.
rules.fix: Cut it and say the honest thing.

rules.message: Setup phrase that delays the point.
rules.fix: Cut it and say the thing.

rules.message: Filler transition.
rules.fix: State the fact directly.

rules.match: at the end of the day
rules.message: Padding cliché.
rules.fix: Cut it.

rules.message: Announces importance instead of showing it.
rules.fix: Say the thing; if it needs a caveat, put the caveat inside the story.

rules.message: Padding before the subject.
rules.fix: Name the subject directly.

rules.message: Corporate jargon the audience doesn't speak.
rules.fix: Use the everyday words the bubble uses.

rules.message: Worn-out cliché.
rules.fix: Describe the concrete action instead.

rules.message: Vague transformation claim.
rules.fix: Say what changed, when and by how much.

rules.message: Clickbait crutch.
rules.fix: State the method or fact plainly.

rules.message: Generic motivational cliché.
rules.fix: Replace it with a concrete action or a real case.

rules.message: Cliché framing ("journey", "embark", "buckle up").
rules.fix: Say what happened, step by step.

rules.message: Vocabulary that reads as machine-written.
rules.fix: Use the plain word the creator would say out loud.

rules.message: Documentary or essay words that break the spoken tone.
rules.fix: Use "and", "so", "but" or a concrete detail.

rules.message: Emphasis crutch with no content.
rules.fix: Delete it; let the fact carry the weight.

rules.message: The text comments on itself instead of moving forward.
rules.fix: Delete the comment and keep the content.

rules.message: Rhetorical question answered right away (Floor FL4).
rules.fix: State the answer as a sentence, with its consequence.

rules.message: Passive voice hides who acts (warning).
rules.fix: Make the person who acts the subject of the sentence.

rules.message: Statistics term for a video result.
rules.fix: Compare with the profile's normal: "3x the profile's normal", "close to normal".

rules.message: Vague claim with no content.
rules.fix: Say what the implication is, concretely.

rules.message: Distant narrator talking about "people".
rules.fix: Put the viewer in the scene with "you".

rules.message: Doubt word that makes the viewer doubt everything (warning).
rules.fix: Keep doubt only where it is real, once, saying who makes the claim.

rules.message: Promises a result the video can't guarantee.
rules.fix: Promise what the video shows, not views, followers or money.

rules.message: The hook opens with a greeting, so the subject arrives late (MC9).
rules.fix: Say the subject and the gain in the first words.

rules.message: Announces the video instead of starting it.
rules.fix: Start with the subject or the scene.

rules.message: Asks for retention instead of earning it.
rules.fix: Open a concrete question the ending answers.

rules.message: Worn-out opener that delays the subject.
rules.fix: State the surprising fact directly, with its source.

rules.message: Generic CTA unrelated to the video's subject.
rules.fix: Continue the subject ("comment {word} and I'll send you {material}") or end without a CTA.

rules.message: The script says a line came from a comment (Floor FL7).
rules.fix: Say the comment as the creator's own line, without quotation marks or metalanguage.

rules.message: "Some people say" turns an audience comment into hearsay (Floor FL7).
rules.fix: Make it the creator's own line, in the comment's words.

rules.message: Attributes a line to followers instead of the creator (Floor FL7).
rules.fix: Say it as the creator's own line.

rules.message: Names the bubble in the script; the audience doesn't need to know it exists.
rules.fix: Speak in the bubble's words without naming it.
